questions.prompt: Which runtime paths should this goal change?
questions.description: The existing daemon already owns /s/<id> session URLs, while the older direct startPlannotatorServer/startReviewServer/startAnnotateServer paths still accept explicit HTML content.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Make all daemon-backed sessions serve the new apps/frontend shell at /s/<sessionId>, while preserving direct non-daemon servers with their current old HTML until a later UI migration.

questions.prompt: How should the daemon serve the frontend build in this phase?
questions.description: The current old apps are bundled as single-file HTML. The new Vite shell currently emits separate asset files unless configured otherwise.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Bundle the frontend shell as a single HTML artifact for daemon serving now. This keeps /s/<id> refreshes reliable, avoids new static-asset routing, and matches the existing release packaging model.

questions.prompt: What UI behavior is in and out of scope for this wiring pass?
questions.description: The shell is intentionally a production-grade skeleton; it can bootstrap sessions and show mode-specific placeholders, but the existing full plan/review/annotate/archive interfaces are not yet migrated into it.
questions.recommendedAnswer: In scope: daemon serves the shell, shell bootstraps against the real daemon APIs, routing works on refresh, build scripts package the shell, and tests prove the integration. Out of scope: migrating the full legacy plan, review, annotate, and archive UIs into the shell.

questions.prompt: What level of verification should this goal require before implementation is considered complete?
questions.description: You said full end-to-end testing does not need to happen in this sequel phase, but the wiring should still be reliable.
questions.recommendedAnswer: Require build/type/lint/tests for apps/frontend, daemon unit/integration tests proving /s/<id> serves shell HTML and /s/<id>/api/session still bootstraps, package/build script coverage, and a focused browser-mode shell test. Do not require a full live daemon plus browser E2E in this phase.
